claim: Yeast studies identified two heterohexameric tethering complexes, which consist of 4 shared (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33) and 2 specific subunits: Vps3 and Vps8 (CORVET) versus Vps39 and Vps41 (HOPS).
source: Yeast studies identified two heterohexameric tethering complexes, which consist of 4 shared (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33) and 2 specific subunits: Vps3 and Vps8 (CORVET) versus Vps39 and Vps41 (HOPS).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior yeast studies and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: CORVET is an early and HOPS is a late endosomal tether.
source: CORVET is an early and HOPS is a late endosomal tether.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research on these tethering complexes.

claim: The function of HOPS is well known in animal cells, while CORVET is poorly characterized.
source: The function of HOPS is well known in animal cells, while CORVET is poorly characterized.
evidence: This represents a summary of the state of knowledge in the field based on prior literature.

claim: Drosophila Vps8 is highly expressed in hemocytes and nephrocytes.
source: Here we show that Drosophila Vps8 is highly expressed in hemocytes and nephrocytes
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and western blots in Figure 1D showing Vps8-HA expression patterns.

claim: Vps8 localizes to early endosomes despite the lack of a clear Vps3 homolog.
source: Here we show that Drosophila Vps8 is highly expressed in hemocytes and nephrocytes, and localizes to early endosomes despite the lack of a clear Vps3 homolog.
evidence: This is supported by colocalization data in Figure 2D,E showing Vps8-HA colocalizing with early endosomal markers Rab5 and Rbsn-5.

claim: Vps8 forms a complex and acts together with Vps16A, Dor/Vps18 and Car/Vps33A.
source: We find that Vps8 forms a complex and acts together with Vps16A, Dor/Vps18 and Car/Vps33A
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 6A, mass spectrometry data in Figure 6C, and colocalization data in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Loss of Vps8, Vps16A, Dor/Vps18, or Car/Vps33A leads to fragmentation of endosomes.
source: loss of any of these proteins leads to fragmentation of endosomes
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figures 5, 7, and 8 showing fragmented late endosomes in mutants.

claim: Vps11 deletion causes enlargement of endosomes, similar to loss of the HOPS-specific subunits Vps39 and Lt/Vps41.
source: Surprisingly, Vps11 deletion causes enlargement of endosomes, similar to loss of the HOPS-specific subunits Vps39 and Lt/Vps41.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence and electron microscopy data in Figures 7 and 8 showing enlarged endosomes in these mutants.

claim: A 4 subunit-containing miniCORVET complex acts as an unconventional early endosomal tether in Drosophila.
source: We thus identify a 4 subunit-containing miniCORVET complex as an unconventional early endosomal tether in Drosophila.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the combination of biochemical, genetic, and localization data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Eukaryotic cells take up extracellular material and transmembrane receptors via endocytosis.
source: Eukaryotic cells take up extracellular material and transmembrane receptors via endocytosis.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cell biology.

claim: Endocytic cargo will either be recycled or degraded in lysosomes.
source: Endocytic cargo will either be recycled or degraded in lysosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about endocytic trafficking pathways.

claim: Early (also known as sorting) endosomes represent the central hub where the decision between recycling and degradation is made.
source: Early (also known as sorting) endosomes represent the central hub where this decision is made.
evidence: This is established knowledge about early endosome function.

claim: Active, GTP-loaded Rabs recruit effectors to vesicular membranes.
source: Active, GTP-loaded Rabs recruit effectors to the vesicular membranes, which then facilitate the subsequent events, including vesicle targeting and homo- and heterotypic fusions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Rab GTPase function, supported by citations.

claim: Tethering complexes and proteins cross-link the membranes of two vesicles/compartments and may promote SNARE complex assembly and fusion.
source: Tethering complexes and proteins cross-link the membranes of the two vesicles/compartments, and may promote SNARE complex assembly and fusion (Hong and Lev, 2014; Kümmel and Ungermann, 2014; Südhof and Rothman, 2009; Wickner and Schekman, 2008; Zick and Wickner, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Four endosomal tethers have been identified to date: Rbsn-5, CORVET, EEA1, and HOPS.
source: Four endosomal tethers have been identified to date: the early endosomal tethers Rbsn-5 (Rabenosyn-5), CORVET (Class C core endosome vacuole tethering), the vertebrate-specific EEA1 (Early endosomal antigen 1), and the late endosomal tether HOPS (Homotypic vacuole fusion and protein sorting).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations.

claim: CORVET binds to Vps21/Rab5 and mediates early endosomal fusions in yeast.
source: CORVET binds to Vps21/Rab5 and mediates early endosomal fusions, whereas HOPS binds to Ypt7/Rab7 and mediates late endosomal, autophagosomal and vacuolar fusions (Balderhaar et al., 2013; Markgraf et al., 2009; Peplowska et al., 2007; Plemel et al., 2011; Rieder and Emr, 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wurmser et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies, supported by multiple citations.

claim: HOPS binds to Ypt7/Rab7 and mediates late endosomal, autophagosomal and vacuolar fusions in yeast.
source: CORVET binds to Vps21/Rab5 and mediates early endosomal fusions, whereas HOPS binds to Ypt7/Rab7 and mediates late endosomal, autophagosomal and vacuolar fusions (Balderhaar et al., 2013; Markgraf et al., 2009; Peplowska et al., 2007; Plemel et al., 2011; Rieder and Emr, 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wurmser et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies, supported by multiple citations.

claim: CORVET and HOPS share a common core of class C Vps proteins (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33).
source: Both share a common core of class C Vps proteins (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33), and the two Rab-binding subunits are located on opposite ends of these complexes (Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural and biochemical studies, supported by citations.

claim: Vps3 and Vps8 are the CORVET specific subunits that bind to Vps21/Rab5.
source: Vps3 and Vps8 are the CORVET specific subunits that bind to Vps21/Rab5, while Vps39 and Vps41 are present in HOPS and interact with Ypt7/Rab7, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies.

claim: Vps39 and Vps41 are present in HOPS and interact with Ypt7/Rab7.
source: Vps3 and Vps8 are the CORVET specific subunits that bind to Vps21/Rab5, while Vps39 and Vps41 are present in HOPS and interact with Ypt7/Rab7, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies.

claim: All HOPS subunits are conserved in metazoans.
source: All HOPS subunits are conserved in metazoans, and the roles of this complex are very similar in mammals and Drosophila to yeast cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge from comparative genomics and functional studies.

claim: The roles of HOPS are very similar in mammals and Drosophila to yeast cells.
source: All HOPS subunits are conserved in metazoans, and the roles of this complex are very similar in mammals and Drosophila to yeast cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge from comparative functional studies.

claim: Two of the genes encoding class C proteins (Vps16 and Vps33) have been duplicated in flies and mammals.
source: Interestingly, two of the genes encoding class C proteins (Vps16 and Vps33) have been duplicated in flies and mammals, but Vps16B/VIPAR and Vps33B have been suggested to form a separate endosomal targeting complex with each other, independent of CORVET or HOPS (van der Kant et al., 2015; Wartosch et al., 2015 ).
evidence: This is established knowledge from genomic and functional studies, supported by citations.

claim: Vps16B/VIPAR and Vps33B form a separate endosomal targeting complex independent of CORVET or HOPS.
source: Interestingly, two of the genes encoding class C proteins (Vps16 and Vps33) have been duplicated in flies and mammals, but Vps16B/VIPAR and Vps33B have been suggested to form a separate endosomal targeting complex with each other, independent of CORVET or HOPS (van der Kant et al., 2015; Wartosch et al., 2015 ).
evidence: This is knowledge from prior studies, supported by citations.

claim: Among the two CORVET-specific subunits only the homologs of Vps8 can be found in higher eukaryotes.
source: Importantly, among the two CORVET-specific subunits only the homologs of Vps8 can be found in higher eukaryotes, as Vps3 seems to be a fungi-specific protein (Klinger et al., 2013; Solinger and Spang, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from comparative genomics, supported by citations.

claim: Vps3 seems to be a fungi-specific protein.
source: Importantly, among the two CORVET-specific subunits only the homologs of Vps8 can be found in higher eukaryotes, as Vps3 seems to be a fungi-specific protein (Klinger et al., 2013; Solinger and Spang, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge from comparative genomics, supported by citations.

claim: One of the mammalian Vps39 homologs, Vps39-2 (also known as Tgfbrap1 or Trap1), can be found in a Vps8-containing CORVET complex.
source: It was recently demonstrated that one of the mammalian Vps39 homologs, Vps39-2 (also known as Tgfbrap1 or Trap1), can be found in a Vps8-containing CORVET complex (Lachmann et al., 2014; Perini et al., 2014).
evidence: This is knowledge from recent mammalian studies, supported by citations.

claim: siRNA knockdown of Vps8 in HeLa cells affects the fusion of only a subset of early endosomes.
source: The function of mammalian CORVET is still poorly characterized: the only functional analysis published to date reported that siRNA knockdown of Vps8 in HeLa cells affects the fusion of only a subset of early endosomes (Perini et al., 2014).
evidence: This is knowledge from a prior mammalian cell study, supported by citation.

claim: HOPS mediates the fusion of lysosomes with endosomes and autophagosomes in Drosophila.
source: Others and we have shown that HOPS mediates the fusion of lysosomes with endosomes and autophagosomes, and also promotes biosynthetic trafficking to lysosomes and lysosome-related organelles such as eye pigment granules (Akbar et al., 2009; Jiang et al., 2014; Lindmo et al., 2006; Pulipparacharuvil et al., 2005; Richardson et al., 2004; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Takáts et al., 2014; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior Drosophila studies, supported by multiple citations.

claim: HOPS promotes biosynthetic trafficking to lysosomes and lysosome-related organelles such as eye pigment granules in Drosophila.
source: Others and we have shown that HOPS mediates the fusion of lysosomes with endosomes and autophagosomes, and also promotes biosynthetic trafficking to lysosomes and lysosome-related organelles such as eye pigment granules (Akbar et al., 2009; Jiang et al., 2014; Lindmo et al., 2006; Pulipparacharuvil et al., 2005; Richardson et al., 2004; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Takáts et al., 2014; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior Drosophila studies, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Vps18 is called Deep orange (Dor) in Drosophila.
source: Several HOPS subunits were named based on the defective eye color of hypomorphic mutant animals: Vps18 is called Deep orange (Dor), Vps33A is Carnation (Car), and Vps41 is known as Light (Lt) in Drosophila (Akbar et al., 2009; Lloyd et al., 1998; Patterson, 1932; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established nomenclature in Drosophila genetics, supported by citations.

claim: Vps33A is called Carnation (Car) in Drosophila.
source: Several HOPS subunits were named based on the defective eye color of hypomorphic mutant animals: Vps18 is called Deep orange (Dor), Vps33A is Carnation (Car), and Vps41 is known as Light (Lt) in Drosophila (Akbar et al., 2009; Lloyd et al., 1998; Patterson, 1932; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established nomenclature in Drosophila genetics, supported by citations.

claim: Vps41 is known as Light (Lt) in Drosophila.
source: Several HOPS subunits were named based on the defective eye color of hypomorphic mutant animals: Vps18 is called Deep orange (Dor), Vps33A is Carnation (Car), and Vps41 is known as Light (Lt) in Drosophila (Akbar et al., 2009; Lloyd et al., 1998; Patterson, 1932; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established nomenclature in Drosophila genetics, supported by citations.

claim: Only a Vps8 homolog can be found in Drosophila, as no gene products show significant similarity to either yeast Vps3 or mammalian Tgfbrap1.
source: Regarding the CORVET-specific subunits, only a Vps8 homolog can be found in Drosophila, as no gene products show significant similarity to either yeast Vps3 or mammalian Tgfbrap1 (Klinger et al., 2013; Li and Blissard, 2015).
evidence: This is knowledge from comparative genomics, supported by citations.

claim: Insect renal system includes garland and pericardial nephrocytes.
source: The insect renal system includes garland and pericardial nephrocytes, which simultaneously show the characteristics of vertebrate renal glomerular podocytes and proximal tubule cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about insect physiology, supported by citations.

claim: Nephrocytes simultaneously show the characteristics of vertebrate renal glomerular podocytes and proximal tubule cells.
source: The insect renal system includes garland and pericardial nephrocytes, which simultaneously show the characteristics of vertebrate renal glomerular podocytes and proximal tubule cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about nephrocyte function, supported by citations.

claim: Nephrocytes utilize a vertebrate-like slit diaphragm and endocytic scavenger receptors to filter the hemolymph.
source: These cells utilize a vertebrate-like slit diaphragm and endocytic scavenger receptors to filter the hemolymph, and store or metabolize the endocytosed material (Weavers et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2013; Zhuang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about nephrocyte function, supported by citations.

claim: The endo-lysosomal compartment fills much of the cytoplasm and forms distinct layers in garland nephrocytes.
source: As a consequence of this continuously high endocytic activity, the endo-lysosomal compartment fills much of the cytoplasm, and forms distinct layers in garland nephrocytes (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Garland nephrocytes are large binucleated cells sheathed with a basal membrane.
source: These large binucleated cells are sheathed with a basal membrane, and the underlying plasma membrane forms numerous lacunae with the slit diaphragm located at the openings.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Clathrin-coated vesicles and early endosomes form under the lacunae in garland nephrocytes.
source: Clathrin-coated vesicles and early endosomes form under the lacunae, and are seen as the Rbsn-5 positive layer in fluorescent photographs (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Alpha-vacuoles are large electron-lucent vesicles that often contain a dense core and are located directly under the early endosomal layer in garland nephrocytes.
source: Under this peripheral layer, large electron-lucent vesicles are found that often contain a dense core. These are also part of the endosomal system, and were traditionally referred to as α-vacuoles (Koenig and Ikeda, 1990; Kosaka and Ikeda, 1983; Rusten et al., 2006). Alpha-vacuoles are the largest vesicles in garland nephrocytes and are located directly under the early endosomal layer, and appear as late, Rab7-positive endosomes in fluorescent images (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2, and by citations to prior studies.

claim: Alpha-vacuoles appear as late, Rab7-positive endosomes in fluorescent images.
source: Alpha-vacuoles are the largest vesicles in garland nephrocytes and are located directly under the early endosomal layer, and appear as late, Rab7-positive endosomes in fluorescent images (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Beta-vacuoles correspond to Lamp1-positive lysosomes in garland nephrocytes.
source: Finally, the perinuclear β-vacuoles correspond to Lamp1-positive lysosomes (Figure 2A,C) (Koenig and Ikeda, 1990; Kosaka and Ikeda, 1983; Rusten et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and by citations to prior studies.

claim: Vps8-HA almost completely colocalizes with the early endosomal markers Rab5 and Rbsn-5.
source: We found that Vps8-HA almost completely colocalizes with the early endosomal markers Rab5 and Rbsn-5 (Figure 2D,E)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2D,E with high Pearson correlation coefficients.

claim: Vps8-HA rarely colocalizes with the late endosomal marker Rab7.
source: but rarely with the late endosomal Rab7 (Figure 2F)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2F with low Pearson correlation coefficient.

claim: Vps8-HA never colocalizes with lysosomal Lamp1.
source: and never with lysosomal Lamp1 (Figure 2G)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 2G with negative Pearson correlation coefficient.

claim: Vps8 may remain on endosomes until they mature into full-size late endosomes.
source: The occasional presence of Vps8 on smaller Rab7-positive late endosomes suggests that Vps8 may remain on endosomes until they mature into full-size late endosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of occasional colocalization with Rab7.

claim: The vps81 mutant contains two small deletions, 4 and 12 base pairs, at the positions targeted by the gRNAs.
source: DNA sequencing identified a mutant line, vps81, which contains two small deletions, 4 and 12 base pairs, respectively, at the positions targeted by the gRNAs (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by DNA sequencing data and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The first deletion in vps81 causes a frameshift and an immediate stop codon, allowing only the first 39 of the 1229 amino acids of the Vps8 protein to be translated.
source: As the first deletion causes a frameshift and an immediate stop codon, only the first 39 of the 1229 amino acids of the Vps8 protein can be translated.
evidence: This is an inference based on the DNA sequencing data showing the frameshift mutation.

claim: The frameshift mutation is present in vps8 transcripts in homozygous vps81/vps81 mutants as well as in vps81/Df animals.
source: Quantitative PCR (qPCR) analysis confirmed that the frameshift mutation is present in vps8 transcripts in homozygous vps81/vps81 mutants as well as in vps81/deficiency (Df) animals, as a primer overlapping the deleted 4 nucleotides failed to amplify the wild type transcript, unlike in control and rescued animals (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The transcript level in vps81/vps81 mutants and in vps81/Df animals decreased to about 25% compared to controls.
source: Indeed, qPCR using primers specific for the non-mutated region of vps8 showed that the transcript level in vps81/vps81 mutants and in vps81/Df animals decreased to about 25% compared to controls, and it was again restored in rescued animals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Vps81 mutant flies are semilethal.
source: Vps81 mutant flies are semilethal: animals can complete metamorphosis, but most of them die as pharate adults (that is, fully formed adult flies that are unable to emerge from the pupal case).
evidence: This is supported by viability data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: 20% of homozygous vps81/vps81 mutants and 16% of vps81/Df animals eclosed.
source: Quantification of viability revealed that 20% of homozygous vps81/vps81 mutants and 16% of vps81/Df animals eclosed, but the resulting adult flies were weak, failed to unfold their wings properly, and died within 24 hr (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is supported by viability quantification data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The eye color of vps8 mutant adult flies was similar to wild type flies.
source: Importantly, the eye color of vps8 mutant adult flies was similar to wild type flies (Figure 3C,C'), unlike hypomorphic HOPS mutants that have a pigmentation defect (Lloyd et al., 1998; Patterson, 1932; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Shestopal et al., 1997; Warner et al., 1998)
evidence: This is supported by photographs shown in Figure 3C,C' and by citations to prior studies on HOPS mutants.

claim: Vps8 functions independent of the HOPS complex in Drosophila.
source: Importantly, the eye color of vps8 mutant adult flies was similar to wild type flies (Figure 3C,C'), unlike hypomorphic HOPS mutants that have a pigmentation defect (Lloyd et al., 1998; Patterson, 1932; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Shestopal et al., 1997; Warner et al., 1998), suggesting that Vps8 functions independent of the HOPS complex in Drosophila.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that vps8 mutants lack the eye pigmentation defect seen in HOPS mutants.

claim: Vps8 mutant larvae had 10-fold more circulating hemocytes than control animals.
source: Vps8 mutant larvae had 10-fold more circulating hemocytes than control animals did, and often contained hemocyte-derived melanotic tumors in their body cavity (Figure 3B,E,E').
evidence: This is supported by hemocyte quantification data shown in Figure 3E,E'.

claim: Vps8 mutant larvae often contained hemocyte-derived melanotic tumors in their body cavity.
source: Vps8 mutant larvae had 10-fold more circulating hemocytes than control animals did, and often contained hemocyte-derived melanotic tumors in their body cavity (Figure 3B,E,E').
evidence: This is supported by photographs shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Loss of Vps8 is accompanied by the disorganization of the sessile hemocyte compartment and the accumulation of crystal cells and lamellocytes.
source: This was accompanied by the disorganization of the sessile hemocyte compartment, and the accumulation of crystal cells and lamellocytes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C) that are only observed in large numbers during immune induction in wild type larvae (Márkus et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C and by citation to prior study.

claim: The semilethality, increased blood cell number and melanotic tumor formation are all rescued by the Vps8-HA transgene.
source: As the semilethality, the increased blood cell number and melanotic tumor formation are all rescued by the Vps8-HA transgene, these indicate that our reporter is functional, and that the observed phenotypes are solely due to the loss of Vps8 function.
evidence: This is supported by rescue data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Hemocyte-derived tumors are also seen in vps16a mutants.
source: Hemocyte-derived tumors are also seen in vps16a mutants, but neither in the HOPS-specific lt mutants nor in vps11 mutants (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is supported by photographs shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Hemocyte-derived tumors are not seen in HOPS-specific lt mutants or in vps11 mutants.
source: Hemocyte-derived tumors are also seen in vps16a mutants, but neither in the HOPS-specific lt mutants nor in vps11 mutants (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is supported by photographs shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Melanotic tumors have been observed for dor mutants.
source: and melanotic tumors have also been observed for dor (Belyaeva et al., 1982).
evidence: This is knowledge from a prior study, supported by citation.

claim: Double mutants of vps8 and lt are similar to vps8 mutants regarding tumor formation.
source: Importantly, double mutants of vps8 and lt are similar to vps8 mutants regarding tumor formation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by photographs shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Visible silver granules are almost absent from vps81/Df mutant nephrocytes.
source: Lysosomal silver deposits are clearly visible as brown granules in garland cells of wild type or rescued animals (Figure 4A,C). In contrast, visible silver granules are almost absent from vps81/Df mutant nephrocytes, indicating impaired silver uptake and/or endo-lysosomal trafficking (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by silver uptake assay data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Vps81/Df cells are able to internalize dextran, but it remains in numerous small vesicles at the periphery of the cells.
source: Vps81/Df cells are also able to internalize dextran, but it remains in numerous small vesicles at the periphery of the cells, pointing to a failure in endosomal trafficking (Figure 4D–F,J, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by dextran uptake assay data shown in Figure 4D-F,J.

claim: Vps8 mutant hemocytes take up FITC labeled bacteria but fail to acidify these endocytic vacuoles.
source: Importantly, hemocytes of control or rescued larvae injected with fluorescently labeled Escherichia coli readily transported the bacteria into acidic, lysosomal compartments, whereas vps81/Df mutants failed to acidify bacteria-containing phagosomes (Figure 4G–I,K).
evidence: This is supported by bacterial uptake assay data shown in Figure 4G-I,K.

claim: Vps8 is required for proper endosomal trafficking in nephrocytes and blood cells.
source: These data altogether indicate that Vps8 is required for proper endosomal trafficking in nephrocytes and blood cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the silver uptake, dextran uptake, and bacterial uptake assay data.

claim: Rab7-positive late endosomes were strongly fragmented in vps8 mutants.
source: In line with this, Rab7-positive late endosomes were strongly fragmented in vps8 mutants: the average size of these vesicles strongly decreased relative to the ones in control or rescued animals (Figure 5A–C,J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5A-C,J.

claim: The distribution of late endosomes is altered in vps8 mutants: Rab7-positive dots almost completely fill the cytoplasm of mutant cells.
source: In addition, the distribution of late endosomes is also altered: Rab7-positive dots almost completely fill the cytoplasm of mutant cells unlike in control or rescued nephrocytes, in which late endosomes form a layer directly beneath peripheral early endosomes (Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: The Rbsn-5 positive early endosomal compartment remains unaffected by the absence of Vps8.
source: Importantly, the Rbsn-5 positive early endosomal compartment remains unaffected by the absence of Vps8, indicating that early endosomes form but are unable to fuse and generate properly sized late endosomes in mutant cells (Figure 5A–C,J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 5A-C,J.

claim: Early endosomes form but are unable to fuse and generate properly sized late endosomes in vps8 mutant cells.
source: Importantly, the Rbsn-5 positive early endosomal compartment remains unaffected by the absence of Vps8, indicating that early endosomes form but are unable to fuse and generate properly sized late endosomes in mutant cells (Figure 5A–C,J, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that early endosomes are normal but late endosomes are fragmented.

claim: Structures positive for LysoTracker Red, Cathepsin L, and LBPA are all fragmented in vps8 mutants.
source: This model is further supported by the distribution of established lysosomal markers: structures positive for LysoTracker Red, for the lysosomal hydrolase Cathepsin L, and for lysobisphosphatidic acid (LBPA) are all fragmented in vps8 mutants (Figure 5D–I).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 5D-I.

claim: Late endosomes and endolysosomes are fragmented in nephrocytes lacking Vps8.
source: Thus, late endosomes and endolysosomes are fragmented in nephrocytes lacking Vps8.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the fragmentation of Rab7, LysoTracker, Cathepsin L, and LBPA positive structures.

claim: Vps8 mutant garland nephrocytes are enlarged compared to wild type or rescued cells.
source: Perhaps as a result of impaired endocytic trafficking, vps8 mutant garland nephrocytes are enlarged compared to wild type or rescued cells (Figure 5A–C,K, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by cell size quantification data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: The endosomal compartment of vps8 mutant wing imaginal discs is indistinguishable from wild type animals.
source: Interestingly, the endosomal compartment of vps8 mutant wing imaginal discs is indistinguishable from wild type animals: both the localization of the internalized Notch receptor, and the size and pattern of Rab7-positive late endosomes are similar to controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vps8 acts as a tissue-specific factor with a critical function in endocytic trafficking in a subset of cells which are highly active in endocytosis.
source: These data raise the possibility that Vps8 acts as a tissue-specific factor with a critical function in endocytic trafficking in a subset of cells, which are highly active in endocytosis (that is, nephrocytes and hemocytes).
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that vps8 mutant phenotypes are strong in nephrocytes and hemocytes but not in wing discs.

claim: Endogenous Car/Vps33A, Dor/Vps18, and Vps16A all interact with Vps8-HA in both adults and larvae.
source: We found that endogenous Car/Vps33A, Dor/Vps18, and Vps16A all interact with Vps8-HA in both adults and larvae (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dor/Vps18 directly binds to Vps8.
source: Moreover, yeast two hybrid experiments showed that Dor/Vps18 directly binds to Vps8 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Vps8-HA colocalized with both myc-tagged Dor/Vps18 and endogenous Vps16A in garland nephrocytes.
source: In line with these, Vps8-HA colocalized with both myc-tagged Dor/Vps18 and endogenous Vps16A in garland nephrocytes (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: A CORVET-like complex exists in flies, despite the lack of clear homologs of either yeast Vps3 or mammalian Tgfbrap1.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that a CORVET-like complex exists in flies, despite the lack of clear homologs of either yeast Vps3 or mammalian Tgfbrap1 (Klinger et al., 2013; Li and Blissard, 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the biochemical interaction and colocalization data, combined with knowledge from comparative genomics.

claim: Vps16A, Dor/Vps18, and Car/Vps33A were detected as very strong interacting partners of Vps8 by mass spectrometry.
source: In line with the western blot data, Vps16A, Dor/Vps18, and Car/Vps33A could all be detected as very strong interacting partners of Vps8 (Figure 6C)
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Neither Vps11 nor Vps39 were detected as interacting partners of Vps8 by mass spectrometry.
source: In line with the western blot data, Vps16A, Dor/Vps18, and Car/Vps33A could all be detected as very strong interacting partners of Vps8 (Figure 6C), but neither Vps11 nor Vps39 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Vps11 might not be a component of the CORVET-like complex in Drosophila.
source: These data suggested that Vps11 might not be a component of this CORVET-like complex in Drosophila that we thus named miniCORVET, consistent with the lack of hemocyte tumors in vps11 mutants (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of Vps11 in the mass spectrometry data and the different phenotype of vps11 mutants.

claim: Late endosomes are fragmented in cells lacking Dor/Vps18, Vps16A or Car/Vps33A, similar to vps8 mutants.
source: As expected, late endosomes are fragmented in cells lacking Dor/Vps18, Vps16A or Car/Vps33A, similar to vps8 mutants (Figure 7A–C,G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7A-C,G.

claim: Nephrocytes lacking the HOPS specific subunits Lt or Vps39 showed extremely enlarged late endosomes.
source: Nephrocytes lacking the HOPS specific subunits Lt or Vps39 showed a very different phenotype: late endosomes were extremely enlarged rather than fragmented, indicating a block of late endosome to lysosome trafficking (Figure 7E,G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7E,G.

claim: Both vps11 mutant and RNAi cells have enlarged late endosomes similarly to loss of HOPS.
source: Importantly, we found that both vps11 mutant and RNAi cells have enlarged late endosomes (Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C) similarly to the loss of HOPS, unlike the fragmentation observed in miniCORVET subunit mutants.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MiniCORVET acts independent of Vps11.
source: This further supports that miniCORVET acts independent of Vps11.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that vps11 mutants have a different phenotype from miniCORVET subunit mutants.

claim: Double mutants for vps8 and lt had fragmented Rab7 vesicles.
source: Double mutants for vps8 and lt had fragmented Rab7 vesicles (Figure 7F,G)
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7F,G.

claim: MiniCORVET is required for the biogenesis of late endosomes while HOPS promotes their clearance.
source: Double mutants for vps8 and lt had fragmented Rab7 vesicles (Figure 7F,G), indicating that miniCORVET is required for the biogenesis of late endosomes while HOPS promotes their clearance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the epistasis analysis showing that vps8 lt double mutants resemble vps8 single mutants.

claim: In all genotypes tested, early endosomes that carry only Rbsn-5 remained unaffected.
source: In all genotypes, early endosomes that carry only Rbsn-5 remained unaffected (Figure 7A–G, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Large α-vacuoles are present in wild type and rescued animals but absent from vps8 mutant cells.
source: As expected from the Rab7 stainings, large α-vacuoles are present in wild type and rescued animals but absent from vps8 mutant cells, which contain only small endosomes (Figure 8A–C,I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8A-C,I.

claim: The endosomal compartment is fragmented and properly sized α-vacuoles are missing from nephrocytes lacking Dor/Vps18, Vps16A, Car/Vps33A, and from cells double mutant for both vps8 and lt.
source: Similarly, the endosomal compartment is fragmented and properly sized α-vacuoles are missing from nephrocytes lacking Dor/Vps18, Vps16A, Car/Vps33A, and also from cells double mutant for both vps8 and lt (Figure 8G–I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8G-I.

claim: Cells lacking both miniCORVET and HOPS function contain lots of small electron-dense lysosome-like organelles.
source: Of note, these cells contain lots of small electron-dense lysosome-like organelles, which are only seen in nephrocytes lacking both miniCORVET and HOPS function.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8G-I and Figure 8—figure supplement 1C-F.

claim: The α-vacuoles of HOPS mutant cells are much larger than those seen in control nephrocytes, and often contain multiple dense cores.
source: In contrast with these, the ultrastructure of nephrocytes lacking the HOPS-specific subunits (Lt/Vps41 or Vps39) as well as the class C protein Vps11 is very similar to each other but greatly different from cells lacking miniCORVET. The α-vacuoles of HOPS mutant cells are much larger than those seen in control nephrocytes, and often contain multiple dense cores (Figure 8D–F,I, Figure 8—figure supplement 1G–I).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8D-F,I.

claim: Multi-core vacuoles with a more electron-dense lumen are found in the perinuclear region of HOPS mutant cells.
source: Multi-core vacuoles with a more electron-dense lumen are also found in the perinuclear region of these cells (Figure 8—figure supplement 1G–I).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1G-I.

claim: The aberrant, enlarged late endosomes and lysosomes in HOPS mutants likely arise from the impaired maturation of late endosomes into degradative lysosomes.
source: These structures likely arise from the impaired maturation of late endosomes into degradative lysosomes in the absence of HOPS function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ultrastructural observations in HOPS mutants.

claim: The formation of enlarged endosomes in HOPS mutants requires miniCORVET.
source: Apparently, the formation of such aberrant, enlarged late endosomes and lysosomes requires miniCORVET, because multiple homotypic endosomal fusion cycles can promote the enlargement of endosomes in HOPS mutants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that double mutants lacking both miniCORVET and HOPS have fragmented rather than enlarged endosomes.

claim: Vps8-HA lost its vesicular localization and became dispersed in the cytoplasm in cells lacking Rab5.
source: As expected from yeast data, Vps8-HA lost its vesicular localization and became dispersed in the cytoplasm in cells lacking Rab5, but not in cells lacking Rab7 (Figure 9A,B, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9A,B.

claim: Vps8-HA did not lose its vesicular localization in cells lacking Rab7.
source: As expected from yeast data, Vps8-HA lost its vesicular localization and became dispersed in the cytoplasm in cells lacking Rab5, but not in cells lacking Rab7 (Figure 9A,B, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Vps8-HA localizes to vesicles containing constitutively active Rab5.
source: We found that Vps8-HA localizes to vesicles containing constitutively active Rab5 (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Vps8-HA preserved its vesicular localization at the periphery of garland nephrocytes overexpressing active Rab7.
source: On the contrary, Vps8-HA preserved its vesicular localization at the periphery of garland nephrocytes overexpressing active Rab7 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The depletion of Dor/Vps18, Car/Vps33A and Vps16A leads to the cytoplasmic dispersion of Vps8-HA.
source: We found that the depletion of Dor/Vps18, Car/Vps33A and Vps16A leads to the cytoplasmic dispersion of Vps8-HA (Figure 9D, Figure 9—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9D and Figure 9—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Vps8 sustains its specific early endosomal localization in cells lacking the HOPS subunits Vps39 or Vps11.
source: In contrast, Vps8 sustains its specific early endosomal localization in cells lacking the HOPS subunits Vps39 or Vps11 (Figure 9E, F).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 9E,F.

claim: Dor/Vps18, Vps16A and Car/Vps33A function together with Vps8 as part of a miniCORVET complex independent of Vps11 and other HOPS-specific subunits.
source: These Vps8-HA localization results provide further evidence that Dor/Vps18, Vps16A and Car/Vps33A function together with Vps8 as part of a miniCORVET complex independent of Vps11 and other HOPS-specific subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the Vps8-HA localization data in various mutant backgrounds.

claim: MiniCORVET colocalizes with Rbsn-5.
source: First, miniCORVET colocalizes with Rbsn-5 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Yeast class C Vps proteins, including Vps18p/Pep3p, interact with Vac1p/Pep7p, the yeast homolog of Rbsn-5.
source: Second, yeast data showed that class C Vps proteins, including Vps18p/Pep3p, interact with Vac1p/Pep7p, the yeast homolog of Rbsn-5 (Peterson and Emr, 2001; Srivastava et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies, supported by citations.

claim: Rbsn-5 shows strong direct interaction with Dor/Vps18 in yeast two hybrid experiments.
source: We therefore analyzed the potential binding of Rbsn-5 to either Dor/Vps18 or Vps8 in yeast two hybrid experiments, and detected its strong direct interaction with Dor/Vps18 (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is supported by yeast two-hybrid data shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Nephrocytes lacking Rbsn-5 contained fragmented Rab7-positive endosomes and were devoid of properly sized α-vacuoles.
source: Importantly, nephrocytes lacking Rbsn-5 also contained fragmented Rab7-positive endosomes and were devoid of properly sized α-vacuoles based on ultrastructural analysis (Figure 10B,C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence and electron microscopy data shown in Figure 10B,C.

claim: The phenotypes of Rbsn-5 mutants are remarkably similar to that of vps8 mutants.
source: These phenotypes are remarkably similar to that of vps8 mutants.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the phenotypes shown in the figures.

claim: Rab5-positive early endosomes were fragmented and accumulated in the perinuclear region in the absence of Rbsn-5, but these endosomes still contained Vps8-HA.
source: Finally, we analyzed the localization of Vps8-HA in cells lacking Rbsn-5. Rab5-positive early endosomes were fragmented and accumulated in the perinuclear region in the absence of Rbsn-5, but these endosomes still contained Vps8-HA (Figurre 10D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: Rbsn-5 acts as an essential early endosomal tether in garland nephrocytes.
source: These results indicate that Rbsn-5 also acts as an essential early endosomal tether in garland nephrocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that loss of Rbsn-5 causes fragmented endosomes similar to loss of miniCORVET.

claim: The endosomal recruitment of Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET appears to be mutually independent of each other.
source: As cells lacking Vps8 have a normal Rbsn-5 positive endosomal compartment (Figure 5A,B), the endosomal recruitment of Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET appears to be mutually independent of each other.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Rbsn-5 localization is normal in vps8 mutants and Vps8 localization is normal in Rbsn-5 mutants.

claim: The formation of properly sized late endosomes and endolysosomes in nephrocytes requires the function of both Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET.
source: Strikingly, the formation of properly sized late endosomes and endolysosomes in nephrocytes thus requires the function of both Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET, which could be explained by their cooperative interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that loss of either Rbsn-5 or miniCORVET causes similar endosomal fragmentation phenotypes.

claim: Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET may cooperate through their cooperative interaction.
source: Strikingly, the formation of properly sized late endosomes and endolysosomes in nephrocytes thus requires the function of both Rbsn-5 and miniCORVET, which could be explained by their cooperative interaction.
evidence: This is speculation based on the direct interaction between Rbsn-5 and Dor, and the similar phenotypes of their mutants.

claim: Rbsn-5 may cooperate with a 4-subunit miniCORVET complex through direct binding to Dor in nephrocytes and hemocytes.
source: We speculate that in this case, Rbsn-5 may cooperate with a 4-subunit miniCORVET complex through direct binding to Dor, an evolutionarily conserved interaction that was reported earlier between the corresponding yeast homologs, Vac1p/Pep7p and Vps18p/Pep3p (Srivastava et al., 2000).
evidence: This is speculation based on the yeast two-hybrid data, colocalization data, and knowledge from yeast studies.

claim: The decreased membrane curvature of large endosomes and phagosomes in nephrocytes and hemocytes may require the contribution of a different tether.
source: This is likely due to the very high endocytic activity of these cells, and perhaps also to their unusually large endosomes and phagosomes, as the decreased membrane curvature may require the contribution of a different tether as well.
evidence: This is speculation about why miniCORVET is particularly important in nephrocytes and hemocytes.

claim: The interaction between Rbsn-5 and Dor is evolutionarily conserved.
source: We speculate that in this case, Rbsn-5 may cooperate with a 4-subunit miniCORVET complex through direct binding to Dor, an evolutionarily conserved interaction that was reported earlier between the corresponding yeast homologs, Vac1p/Pep7p and Vps18p/Pep3p (Srivastava et al., 2000).
evidence: This is knowledge from prior yeast studies, supported by citation.

claim: Vps8 appears to act independent of Vps11 in Drosophila.
source: Perhaps the most surprising aspect of our study is that Vps8 appears to act independent of Vps11 in Drosophila.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: A recent pulldown study identified Vps8, Car, Dor and Vps16A in a search for Rab5 effectors in Drosophila cells, but not Vps11, Vps39 or Lt.
source: Our data go along with those of a recent pulldown study, which identified Vps8, Car, Dor and Vps16A in a search for Rab5 effectors in Drosophila cells, but not Vps11, Vps39 or Lt (Gillingham et al., 2014).
evidence: This is knowledge from a prior study, supported by citation.

claim: Vps11 was found in a Rab2 pulldown experiment along with the other 5 HOPS subunits, unlike Vps8.
source: Importantly, Vps11 was found in a Rab2 pulldown experiment along with the other 5 HOPS subunits, unlike Vps8 (Gillingham et al., 2014).
evidence: This is knowledge from a prior study, supported by citation.

claim: HOPS and CORVET can be divided into two separate parts: a head part and a tail part.
source: HOPS and CORVET can be divided into two separate parts: a head part composed of the class C proteins Vps33, Vps16, Vps18, and the CORVET or HOPS specific proteins Vps8 or Vps41, respectively. The tail part contains the class C protein Vps11, and Vps3 or Vps39 for CORVET or HOPS, respectively (Bröcker et al., 2012; Ostrowicz et al., 2010; van der Kant et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from structural studies, supported by citations.

claim: An approximately 200 residue region near the Vps11 C-terminus is necessary and sufficient to hold Vps3 or Vps39 onto the rest of the class C Vps core in yeast.
source: An approximately 200 residue region near the Vps11 C-terminus is necessary and sufficient to hold Vps3 or Vps39 onto the rest of the class C Vps core in yeast (Ostrowicz et al., 2010; Plemel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from yeast studies, supported by citations.

claim: A miniCORVET corresponding to the head part of the yeast or mammalian CORVET complexes exists in Drosophila.
source: We thus propose that unlike a fully formed HOPS complex, a miniCORVET corresponding to the head part of the yeast or mammalian CORVET complexes exist in Drosophila.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from all the data presented.

claim: Recruitment of the SM protein Car/Vps33A may facilitate the fusion of early endosomes by acting as a template for SNARE assembly.
source: In addition to its tethering function, recruitment of the SM (Sec1/Munc18) protein Car/Vps33A may also facilitate the fusion of early endosomes by acting as a template for SNARE assembly (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation based on knowledge about SM protein function, supported by citation.

claim: MiniCORVET acts upstream of HOPS.
source: Taken together, we identify the novel 4-subunit miniCORVET complex as a tether for early endosomes that is essential for endocytic trafficking in nephrocytes and hemocytes in Drosophila, and show that it acts upstream of HOPS, which mediates the fusion of lysosomes with late endosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the epistasis analysis showing that vps8 lt double mutants resemble vps8 single mutants.

claim: HOPS mediates the fusion of lysosomes with late endosomes.
source: Taken together, we identify the novel 4-subunit miniCORVET complex as a tether for early endosomes that is essential for endocytic trafficking in nephrocytes and hemocytes in Drosophila, and show that it acts upstream of HOPS, which mediates the fusion of lysosomes with late endosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior studies and supported by the data in this manuscript.
